caveats: Source is a Codex session rollout log (~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-*.jsonl), not `codex exec --json` stdout. The rollout line is `{type: 'event_msg', payload: {type: 'task_complete', error: {message, codex_error_info}}}`.

The runtime parser codex-exec-json-v1 reads `{type: 'turn.failed', error: {message}}` and `{type: 'error', message}` from `exec --json` stdout (src/runtime/worker/parsers.ts). It does not read the rollout shape. No `exec --json` capture of this error exists, so that the same message text arrives on `exec --json` is an inference, not an observation.
Only the phrase `usage limit` appears in this transcript. `rate limit`, `quota exceeded`, `too many requests` and `resource_exhausted` are not supported by it and stay unverified.
The rollout was recorded by a codex-cli whose version was not stored in the line; cliVersion is the version installed when this record was made.
masking: The one JSON line holding the error message was copied alone from the session log. timestamp, turn ids, ordinal and the numeric timing fields are replaced by fixed placeholders; the message text, event type names and key names are kept as recorded. No other line of the log was read into this file.
